subject: research/capture-learngate
professional: a senior image-based-rendering / novel-view-synthesis researcher (the kind who reviews for CVPR or SIGGRAPH). They would check first that the scene, stereo and warp are geometrically right, that the hand-set baseline was tuned as hard as the learned model, that the gain survives a different training seed, that prior learned-blending work is cited, and whether PSNR alone on a toy scene supports the conclusion

evidence.correctness: Rerun in a scratch copy (`PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py`) reproduces experiments/results.txt byte for byte, and figure.py reproduces bystanders.svg identically. Independent checks (indep.py, my own scalar look-at pinhole + ray/plane + ray/cylinder tracer, scipy, scikit-image, scikit-learn): render depth matches my tracer to 3.6e-14 m on 2,192 random pixels with no sky/hit mismatches; the block matcher's disparity matches analytic F*b/z (F=166.277) with median error 0.14 to 0.16 px; psnr equals skimage peak_signal_noise_ratio(data_range=1) to 6 decimals; ideal_weight equals scipy bounded argmin of the per-pixel squared error to 2e-8; Ridge matches sklearn Ridge to 4e-5 (lam=1) and 4e-3 (lam=100, it also penalises the intercept). Derived numbers (headroom 2.71, shares 0.148/0.288/0.358, stress 0.46 of 1.61, +0.13 over fill) recompute. Robustness (fair.py): a 400-point soft-gate sweep over t0, t1, grow and smooth finds train 26.352 vs the committed grid's 26.331 and test 26.209 vs 26.206, so the baseline was not under-tuned; MLP seeds 0, 1, 2 give test 26.780/26.780/26.782 and +0.571 to +0.573 dB over the better-tuned soft gate, 40/40 ahead each. Not 4: PSNR only, toy scene.

Live page https://marisstella.app/research/capture-learngate/ not checked: the session proxy returned 403 on CONNECT. README says run.py takes 'about 2.5 minutes'; it took 13 min 42 s wall here, but under concurrent load from my other checks, so not scored as a defect. Next steps are honestly marked undone (capture-whichwrong has since taken two of them).
evidence.verification: `cd research/capture-learngate && python3 -m pytest -q tests`: 7 passed in 0.60 s. The tests cover ideal_weight, the texture seed, feature shape, Ridge on a linear target, MLP beating Ridge on an interaction, and output range. Four seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 1 caught (tanh derivative 1-a^2 -> 1-a, by the MLP test), 3 survived: stereo depth F*b/disp -> F*b/(disp+1) (stereo.py:53), near_hole feature built from the wrong source mask (learn.py:47), and the soft gate losing its grow step (hybrid.py:101). Nothing tests the stereo matcher, the warp, the gates, the feature values or any committed result; only a full 2.5+ minute rerun and diff would notice.
evidence.craft: Read scene.py, stereo.py, synth.py, hybrid.py, learn.py, run.py, figure.py, tests. Numpy-only, vectorised, deterministic seeds, results parsed into the figure rather than retyped. Defects: scene, stereo, synth and hybrid are copied from capture-softgate (hybrid.py is byte-identical to research/capture-softgate/src/capture_softgate/hybrid.py), the 'copied engines' pattern across the capture-* family; learn.blend (learn.py:126) is dead code, run.py reimplements it as render_with; Ridge penalises the intercept (learn.py:78, non-standard); run.py defines a class inside the ablation loop; pyproject.toml description is the copied capture-softgate one ('Confidence-gated fallback and hole filling'), not this project.
evidence.claims: Every headline number (26.78/26.21/25.81, +0.57 se 0.05, 40/40, 0.36/0.15/0.29 of 2.7 dB, stress +0.24 and 24/25, by-bystander table, ablation figures, 'MLP 0.19 above ridge', '0.13 above filling') is in results.txt and recomputes. Limitations are specific and candid (toy scene, same-family textures, PSNR only, unequal capacity, 10 validation configs, fixed holes). Small overstatements: 'raw nearest camera' when the target is the exact midpoint so the two sources are equidistant and 'nearest' is just the first after a tie-breaking sort (run.py:46,53); hybrid.py:9 and the table call the binary oracle an upper bound, but it picks per pixel by L1 and is scored by L2, so it is not the PSNR-optimal binary choice. Neither changes a headline.
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher who wants to know whether learned per-pixel blend weights beat a hand-set disagreement ramp for two-view stereo-depth synthesis, and to build on it. It is reproducible, deterministic and was built on (capture-whichwrong). But the nearest prior work makes the result unsurprising and not new: view-dependent blending weights (Buehler et al., Unstructured Lumigraph Rendering, SIGGRAPH 2001), learned per-pixel blending weights from warped mosaics (Hedman et al., Deep Blending for Free-Viewpoint IBR, SIGGRAPH Asia 2018), Soft3D (Penner & Zhang 2017), DeepStereo (Flynn et al. 2016) and Free View Synthesis (Riegler & Koltun, ECCV 2020) all learn or derive blend weights with far richer inputs. None is cited; README:9 says only that it is 'ordinary in learned image-based rendering'. A +0.57 dB PSNR gain on an analytic cylinder scene with a block matcher is sound as an internal measurement but does not transfer, and the project is not part of a programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md. Well short of the PhD bar.
evidence.domain: Against IBR evaluation practice (PSNR plus SSIM and LPIPS on standard multi-view datasets, e.g. the protocols of Hedman 2018 and Riegler & Koltun 2020): PSNR only (disclosed), one analytic scene family, no perceptual or seam metric, and 0.5 dB may be invisible (disclosed). The method itself (regress the closed-form least-squares weight with an image-loss weighting, tune baselines on the same training configs, held-out textures, an out-of-range stress split, ablation) is sound and the baseline-tuning is fair as my wider sweep shows. The binary oracle uses an L1 choice under an L2 score, and the 'nearest camera' is a tie at the midpoint. A reviewer would accept it as a careful toy study and reject it as a contribution.

verdict: A careful, honest toy study whose numbers are right and robust. results.txt and the figure reproduce byte for byte; the scene geometry matches an independent ray tracer to 1e-14 m, the matcher's disparity matches F*b/z to 0.15 px, and PSNR, the least-squares blend weight and Ridge agree with scikit-image, scipy and scikit-learn. The headline +0.57 dB over the soft gate survives a 400-point re-tuning of that gate (it gains 0.003 dB) and three MLP seeds (40/40 each time). It misses the bar on verification (3 of 4 seeded mutants survive; nothing tests the stereo, warp, gates or results) and on the research bar: the idea of learned per-pixel blend weights is established IBR practice (Hedman 2018, Riegler & Koltun 2020) and none of it is cited, the evaluation is PSNR only on an analytic cylinder scene, and the copied engines from capture-softgate are a maintenance smell. Minor overstatements: the 'nearest' camera is a tie at the midpoint, and the binary oracle is not an L2 bound.
